content.user_title: Guide Stella Through Her Final Choice
content.value_statement: A story finale needs meaningful choices without losing emotional closure. This skill guides a branching conversation about returning home, staying on Gaia, or building a connection between both worlds.
actual_capabilities: Sets the final chapter context for Stella Chen on Gaia.
Presents return, stay, and bridge-between-worlds story paths.
Guides a reflective discussion of prior events and relationships.
Provides dialogue beats for rescue, ship repair, and farewell scenes.
Supports multiple endings based on player advice and earlier choices.
limitations: It is a narrative guide, not a complete game engine.
It does not track earlier chapter choices automatically.
It does not create artwork, sound, or interactive software.
The supplied dialogue mixes Chinese and English.

use_cases.title: Finish a campaign finale
use_cases.description: Use the chapter structure to conclude a long-running science-fiction roleplay with a meaningful player choice.

use_cases.title: Write branching ending scenes
use_cases.description: Adapt the return, stay, and ambassador paths into a game or visual novel ending.

use_cases.title: Practice emotional character dialogue
use_cases.description: Explore how a transformed survivor weighs family, duty, friendship, and a new home.

prompt_templates.title: Start the finale
prompt_templates.prompt: Start Planning the Escape. Stella has received a rescue signal. Present her mixed feelings and ask what I think she should do.

prompt_templates.title: Choose to return home
prompt_templates.prompt: Guide Stella toward returning to Earth. Include a farewell to Gaia and a promise to protect the Eos people.

prompt_templates.title: Choose a new life
prompt_templates.prompt: Guide Stella toward staying on Gaia. Show her decision clearly and include her message to Mission Control.

prompt_templates.title: Build the ambassador ending
prompt_templates.prompt: Create the bridge-between-worlds ending. Use earlier discoveries, Eos friendships, and practical concerns to make the plan believable.

output_examples.input: Stella receives a rescue signal after months on Gaia.
output: Stella recognizes the signal as proof that Earth has not forgotten her.
She looks at her research station and asks whether returning still feels like going home.

output_examples.input: The player advises Stella to stay with the Eos.
output: Stella sends Mission Control a calm message that she is alive and choosing to remain.
She begins planning a permanent research station with the Eos.
Stella decides to return as an ambassador and seek respectful contact between Earth and Gaia.
The ending frames her decision as a new beginning rather than a final goodbye.

best_practices: Ask the player about earlier choices before selecting an ending path.
Treat every ending as valid and avoid presenting one choice as morally correct.
Give Stella time to reflect before asking for the player response.
anti_patterns: Do not force a choice before the player has discussed its consequences.
Do not ignore established events from earlier chapters.
Do not reduce the ending to action without emotional closure.

faq.question: What is this skill for?
faq.answer: It guides the final chapter of a science-fiction roleplay about Stella Chen and Gaia.

faq.question: Can Stella return to Earth?
faq.answer: Yes. The skill includes an ending where Stella returns and speaks for Gaia and the Eos.

faq.question: Can Stella remain on Gaia?
faq.answer: Yes. She can choose a permanent life on Gaia and continue her research.

faq.question: Is there a compromise ending?
faq.answer: Yes. Stella can return to Earth and plan a respectful future expedition to Gaia.

faq.question: Does the skill remember earlier chapters?
faq.answer: No. Provide relevant earlier choices in your prompt so the conversation can use them.

faq.question: Which languages does the source use?
faq.answer: The source dialogue mixes Chinese and English.
